clue.text: Horse fly problem returns

indicators.note: returns tells us the fly and the problem, set side by side, are read back to front together

parts.note: a gnat is a small fly
a sum is an arithmetic problem

explanation.surface: A horse is plagued again and again by flies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returns' turns the whole of GNAT + SUM, giving the run backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A wild horse of the American plains is called by this name.

clue.text: They're lucky, of course, in literary work

indicators.note: in means the course is set inside the literary work

parts.note: MS is a manuscript, a writer's work
Ascot is a racecourse in Berkshire

explanation.surface: Lucky things, naturally, appear in a book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of course' reads as naturally, but ASCOT is the racecourse; 'of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Charms or creatures kept to bring good luck.

clue.text: This should hold the beaver in play

definitions.text: This should hold the beaver in play

parts.words: This should hold the beaver in play
parts.note: beaver is old slang for a beard; in a stage play an actor's false beard is stuck on with a theatrical adhesive

explanation.surface: Something to keep a beaver from escaping during a game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beaver' suggests the animal, but it is slang for a beard, and 'play' is a stage play.
explanation.definitionFit: A theatrical adhesive used to attach false hair to an actor's face.

clue.text: Former price for spirit

explanation.surface: What someone once paid for a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: An old gold coin, once the customary fee to a lawyer or physician; also a heavenly being.

clue.text: Find me filling new storage fuel-container

indicators.note: filling means me goes inside the rearranged letters
new means storage is made into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: Locate me inside a new store, then a container for fuel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' turns STORAGE into GASOTER, and 'filling' puts ME inside it; 'Find' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A large tank holding town gas for supply to homes.

clue.text: Related to business agent, possibly

parts.note: Co. is the abbreviation for company, a business

indicators.note: possibly suggests the word agent may appear in some other arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone is connected to a business agent, perhaps by family.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges AGENT to GNATE, placed after CO; 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Words or relatives sharing a common origin are said to be akin in this way.

clue.text: Message from the tower?

parts.note: a tower here is something that tows, using a strong rope; the same word names a telegram

explanation.surface: A message sent from a tall tower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tower' looks like a tall building but means one that tows.
explanation.definitionFit: A telegram; also a heavy towing rope.

clue.text: Bird and I fill bird book up

indicators.note: fill means I goes inside the second bird

parts.note: a gull is a seabird

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the book is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a tome is a large book

explanation.surface: A bird and I stuff a bird book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fill' puts I inside GULL for GUILL; 'up' turns TOME to EMOT; 'and' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A seabird of the auk family that nests on cliff ledges.

clue.text: Foreigner has a right to join

parts.note: a lien is a legal right to hold property until a debt is paid

explanation.surface: An immigrant has the right to become a member.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has' and 'to join' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: A person from another country.

clue.text: Man reforms T.U.C. with ease

indicators.note: reforms means the letters are formed again into a new order

parts.note: TUC is the Trades Union Congress

explanation.surface: A man reorganises the trade union body with ease.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reforms' rearranges TUC and EASE; 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A male first name.

clue.text: Music corrected by the golf pro ?

explanation.surface: A golf professional puts a player's music right.
explanation.definitionFit: A jazz style of the big-band era; also the stroke a golf coach adjusts for a pupil.

clue.text: Settles about one form of grants

indicators.note: about means the first word's synonym goes around the second

parts.note: to subside is to sink or settle
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone sorts out one type of grant.
explanation.definitionFit: Payments of state aid to an industry or cause are a kind of grant.

clue.text: Banner of a Rome film-producer

indicators.note: a producer makes something, here a new arrangement from the letters before it

parts.note: taken as written as anagram material

explanation.surface: The banner credits a film producer based in Rome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'producer', read as a maker, rearranges A ROME FILM into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The sacred red standard of the early French kings, so any rallying flag.

clue.text: Jenny meets a girl

parts.note: Jenny Lind was the famous Swedish soprano, the 'Swedish Nightingale'

explanation.surface: A girl called Jenny meets another girl.
explanation.definitionFit: A common female first name.

clue.text: Sad blow to transport leader, in our view

parts.note: a sigh is a sad breath blown out

indicators.note: leader picks the opening letter of the word transport

explanation.surface: A sad setback for a transport boss, in our opinion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sad blow' looks like a misfortune, but it is a breath let out in sorrow; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: What is within our field of vision is what we can see.

clue.text: Sect assembled in high building in Northants

indicators.note: in means the reassembled sect goes inside the high building

parts.note: a tower is a tall building

indicators.note: assembled means the letters of sect are put together in a new order

explanation.surface: A sect has gathered in a tall building in Northamptonshire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'assembled' gives CEST, put by the first 'in' inside TOWER. Northants is Northamptonshire, an English county.
explanation.definitionFit: Towcester is a market town in Northamptonshire.

clue.text: Indian carving given to archbishop — nothing in that!

indicators.note: in that puts nothing inside the archbishop just named

parts.note: William Temple was Archbishop of Canterbury in the 1940s
O is the zero, nothing

explanation.surface: An Indian carving is presented to an archbishop, who finds nothing in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in that' places O inside TEMPLE, giving TEMPOLE after TO; 'given' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A carved post of North American Indian peoples showing clan emblems.

clue.text: Will be opened by the vicar ?

explanation.surface: A will is to be opened by the parson.
explanation.definitionFit: A legal will; also the Old or New division of the Bible, which the parson opens to read.

clue.text: Beast our nag contrived to beat

indicators.note: contrived means our nag is rearranged by design

parts.note: to tan is to beat, as in tan someone's hide

explanation.surface: An animal our horse was made to beat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'contrived' turns OUR NAG into ORANGU; 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A great ape of Borneo and Sumatra.

clue.text: Direction for returning prodigal — to back one pools result among others

indicators.note: among means one piece is set within the other

parts.note: on the football pools the other results are homes (home wins) and aways

indicators.note: back means the pools result is read in reverse

parts.note: a draw is one of the results forecast on the football pools

explanation.surface: Guidance to the prodigal son coming home, mixed up with betting on football pools.
explanation.walkthrough: The football pools are a British betting game forecasting match results as homes, aways and draws. 'back' turns DRAW to WARD, set among HOMES; 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The prodigal son of the parable goes back to his father's house, so his way is towards home.

clue.text: Shelter given up to someone lacking possessions

parts.note: a haven is a refuge

indicators.note: up in a down clue means to is read upward, backwards

explanation.surface: Refuge is surrendered to a pauper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'given' is a link; 'up' turns TO to OT.
explanation.definitionFit: A poor person, set against the wealthy who have.

clue.text: Characteristic of cup-bearer, say ?

indicators.note: say means the word for a cup-bearer is spoken, giving a similar sound

parts.note: a tray carries cups

explanation.surface: Asking what quality marks a royal cupbearer.
explanation.walkthrough: In British speech the answer is said like TRAY, with the final T silent.
explanation.definitionFit: A distinguishing quality of a person's character.

clue.text: Parry's predecessors ?

parts.note: Parry looks like a surname, but in fencing a parry is the block that follows each lunge

explanation.surface: Asking who came before someone named Parry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Parry's' looks like a person's name; it is the fencing move.
explanation.definitionFit: Lunging attacks with a sword come before the defender's block.

clue.text: Some trouble over needy writer

indicators.note: some means only part of the following words is taken

explanation.surface: A writer in need runs into trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: Jules Verne was the French author of science-fiction novels.

clue.text: King's daughter seen about on horseback

parts.note: re means about, concerning

indicators.note: back, the end of horseback, means the horse word is read in reverse

parts.note: a nag is a horse

explanation.surface: A princess is spotted riding about on horseback.
explanation.walkthrough: 'horseback' splits into horse and back: NAG turned gives GAN, set under RE ('on' in a down clue); 'seen' is a link. Regan is one of King Lear's daughters.
explanation.definitionFit: Regan is the second daughter of Shakespeare's King Lear.

clue.text: Anger after vessels return from port

indicators.note: after puts anger behind the reversed vessels
return means the vessels word is read backwards

parts.note: vats are large vessels

explanation.surface: Someone flies into a rage after the boats come back from harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'return' turns VATS to STAV; 'from' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Stavanger is a seaport in south-west Norway.

clue.text: Saw poor Mr. Turner climb ?

indicators.note: poor means the following letters are in poor shape, so reworked
a turner is one who turns, here turning saw and Mr into new order

explanation.surface: I saw poor Mr Turner climbing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turner' looks like the painter's name but is one who turns letters; 'poor' also signals the rearrangement of SAW and MR.
explanation.definitionFit: To shin up a tree or rope is to climb.

clue.text: River girl-non-starter

parts.note: Anna is a girl's name

indicators.note: starter takes the opening letter of the word non

explanation.surface: A river girl who never gets going.
explanation.definitionFit: The Annan is a river in south-west Scotland.

clue.text: Nearly a term doing revision — horrifying experience !

parts.note: nigh means nearly, as in well-nigh

indicators.note: doing revision means the words a term are revised into new order

explanation.surface: A student facing a term of revision has a dreadful time.
explanation.definitionFit: A terrifying dream, and so any frightening ordeal.

clue.text: Records in the case ?

explanation.surface: Records kept in a case.
explanation.definitionFit: Written jottings; also banknotes, carried in a wallet called a notecase.

clue.text: Brown Trumpet the favourite is off with a spirited burst

parts.note: tan is a light brown

indicators.note: is off means the favourite is removed from the trumpet

parts.note: a pet is a favourite

explanation.surface: A brown trumpet goes missing and a fit of temper follows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is off' takes PET from TRUMPET, leaving TRUM; 'with a' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An outburst of bad temper, like a child's fit of rage.

clue.text: Cross with workers who pay the rent?

parts.note: X is a cross and the Roman numeral for ten
worker ants are the classic workers of crosswords

explanation.surface: Angry with the workers who pay the rent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross' looks like angry, but it is the X shape, ten in Roman numerals.
explanation.definitionFit: Occupiers who rent a property from a landlord.
